author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites [Ketubot 51a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.51b.18-19) for the report that he was a bandit who conquered towns and ruled them. At the [end of Terumot chapter 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.8.4.13), Hyman says Queen Zenobia told Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Shmuel, “With this sword Bar Netzer killed,” etc. See [Bereshit Rabbah 76:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.76.6).

notes.text: The consulted Terumot paragraph has an entering Saracen say that Bar Netzer killed his brother with this sword. Hyman instead assigns the abbreviated statement to Zenobia. The source’s active “killed” is retained; “was killed” was a mistranslation. The speaker discrepancy remains open.

The linked Yerushalmi calls the rabbis Imi and Shmuel. Zenobia addresses them about divine intervention. It is the next speaker, a Saracen carrying a sword, who says Bar Nitzor killed his brother with it. The wording leaves whose brother open.

[Hyman’s printed notice](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3f/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._I._1910.pdf#page=306) cites 51a, while the linked discussion of Ben Netzer as king and bandit is at 51b. [Rashi there](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Ketubot.51b.18.2) says he conquered and ruled towns. The scan reads קטיל and the supplied transcription has קטל. The linked midrash identifies Ben Netzer with the small horn in one interpretation of Daniel; Rabbi Yochanan gives a different interpretation.
